open_obligations: Check whether Smit et al.'s Society of Minds matches Du et al.'s prompts and rounds.
Check how Smit et al.'s datasets compare with the tasks Du et al. use.
Check whether Smit et al.'s comparisons with other protocols are compute-matched.

Note that the cited Du et al. passage calls debate a complementary approach and reports gains without comparing it with other prompting strategies such as Medprompt, so Smit et al.'s result limits only a claim that debate beats those strategies; the passages do not show whether it contradicts Du et al.'s reported gains.
Before proposing CHALLENGES, check Smit et al.'s Table 2 rows for whether the debating protocols fail to beat the single-agent baseline on the reasoning datasets.
in.other_title: No protocol dominates all datasets; debate does not win on reasoning datasets
in.rationale: Du et al. report multi-agent debate improves reasoning and factuality, and present it as a complementary approach. Smit et al. report no protocol dominates on all datasets, Medprompt seems to perform best overall, and the debating protocols do not outperform the other protocols on the reasoning datasets. Both discuss whether multi-agent debate helps LLM reasoning, but the cited Du et al. passage compares debate with no other prompting protocol, and the cited Smit et al. lines compare the debating protocols with the other protocols as a group without showing a debating protocol failing to improve over a single agent, so neither bears on the other's claim and the link is navigation only.
in.scope: proposed SHARES_TOPIC: multi-agent debate as a way to improve LLM reasoning, which Du et al. report gains from and Smit et al. compare with other prompting protocols

text: The paper proposes that multiple instances of a language model propose answers and then debate their responses and reasoning over several rounds until they reach a common final answer. The authors report that this improves mathematical and strategic reasoning on several tasks and improves factual validity, reducing hallucinated answers, using only black-box access and the same prompts across tasks.
title: Multiagent debate between LLM instances improves reasoning and factual accuracy
